note: Routing evals. The suite is invoked EXPLICITLY — no skill here fires from a matched description, so this is NOT a trigger test. Each prompt asks: given the suite has already been invoked, which skill should the run route to? Run by giving each prompt to `engineer` (its step-5 intent classifier) or to the root SKILL.md routing table, and checking where it routes. `expected: none` means no phase applies — answer the user directly. The `why` calls out collision-prone near-misses.
status: EXECUTED 2026-08-29 against v0.2.1 (29 cases). Result: 28 routed as expected; case 15 was WRONG and has been corrected — it expected `discover` for 'is our feature set enough', which contradicts discover's own boundary rule naming that assess's question. Near-misses confirmed correct: case 18 ('design the database schema') routes to `define` not `design`, and case 19 ('plan our Q3 roadmap') routes to `discover` not `blueprint` — both disambiguated by the skill descriptions as written. Method: each prompt judged against the root SKILL.md routing table plus each skill's description and stated boundaries. Still not automated in CI: validate.py only checks that this file parses.

evals.prompt: build a full Next.js todo app, frontend and backend, with a nice UI
evals.why: from-scratch multi-step build, no plan yet → orchestrator, NOT construct

evals.prompt: implement the rate-limit middleware task from our plan
evals.why: already-planned single task → construct, NOT engineer

evals.prompt: continue where we left off on the auth feature

evals.why: trivial one-liner → construct directly, NOT engineer/define

evals.prompt: I want to build a booking system but I'm not sure what it should do yet
break the approved spec into an ordered set of tasks
does the checkout flow actually work? run the tests
there's a bug: totals are off by one cent sometimes
review my PR for bugs, security, and performance before I merge
is this API endpoint's error handling any good?
ship it to production
make this dashboard screen look more premium and polished
audit this settings page's UI — spacing, hierarchy, accessibility
evals.why: UI review → design, NOT inspect (which is code review)

evals.prompt: what should we build next for our SaaS — any feature ideas?
scan competitors and tell me if our feature set is enough
evals.why: COMPOUND ask. `discover`'s own boundary rule is explicit: "if the real question is 'are our existing features good enough?', that's assess". The sufficiency judgment leads, and assess hands its Recommended next moves to discover. Corrected from `discover` when these evals were first executed (v0.2.2) — the case predated the boundary rule and had drifted.
